messages:
Mia Chen: noticing the ingestion SLO burn spike in grafana — 99th pct latency for /telemetry/write jumped across us-west and eu-central around 02:10 UTC
Devin Patel: saw that, looked noisy. is this per-tenant or global?
Mia Chen: looks like a mix. global 99p went from ~250ms to ~1.2s, but a handful of tenants show long tails ~3-5s.
Jordan Lee: do we have the raw Prom queries? could be histogram bucket skew from different scrape intervals or a label cardinality issue.
Mia Chen: current chart uses: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(telemetry_ingest_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant_id, region))`
Devin Patel: ah, tenant_id in the by() — that explodes series. Might be causing partial rollups and missing series on some ingestion nodes.
Paul Rivers: agreed. high cardinality + sharded remote write can create gaps. we should either drop tenant_id for global SLO or use a recording rule to pre-aggregate per-tenant with relabeling.
Mia Chen: any recommended recording rule?
Jordan Lee: something like:
```
- name: telemetry_ingest:latency:rate1m
  expr: sum by (le, region, tenant_bucket) (rate(telemetry_ingest_latency_seconds_bucket[1m]))
```
where tenant_bucket is a relabeled low-cardinality bucket of tenant tier (free/premium/enterprise) instead of raw id.
Devin Patel: +1. relabeling to tenant_tier reduces cardinality and keeps SLI meaningful for error budgets.
Mia Chen: but we also need accurate per-tenant billing impact for dedicated customers. dropping tenant_id loses that fidelity.
Paul Rivers: keep a separate per-tenant high-card series for short retention (7d) sent to cost analytics; use the low-cardinality SLI series for long-term SLO reporting and alerts. tradeoff: retention and storage cost vs alert fidelity.
infra-bot: alert: SLO-burn-telemetry-ingest US-WEST spike @ 2024-11-12T02:11:05Z (severity: page)
Mia Chen: paging oncall already did. question for ops: can we throttle or route heavy tenants to dedicated ingestion pools to protect platform SLO?
Devin Patel: we can route by tenant_tier in the gateway and enforce per-tenant qps caps. that would reduce transient saturation but needs rollout plan.
Jordan Lee: also validate scrape and push intervals. I suspect a batch of large telemetry payloads upstream caused longer processing per RPC, inflating tail which then skews histogram buckets.
Mia Chen: good point. traces show a retry storm from a single IP range hitting a few ingestion pods.
Paul Rivers: for alert tuning: let's change the SLO alert to require sustained burn: `slo_burn_rate > 2x for 12m and sustained errorbudget_loss > 0.5%` instead of immediate page on single 5m spike. reduces noisy pages.
Devin Patel: we should also add a burn smoothing function in the dashboard: 5m raw, 30m exponential smoothing for paging decisions.
Mia Chen: agree. can someone draft the alert patch and a short runbook block?
Jordan Lee: I'll open a PR for the recording rule + dashboard panel to show raw vs downsampled 99p and tenant-tier split.
Paul Rivers: I'll draft the alert tweak and runbook note about dedicated routing + short retention per-tenant metrics for billing.
Mia Chen: thanks. timeline?
Jordan Lee: PR by EOD, canary to staging tomorrow morning.
Paul Rivers: alert patch in 2 hours, will post diff here.
Mia Chen: assigning follow-ups: Jordan (recording rules + dashboard), Paul (alert + runbook), Devin (gateway rate cap feasibility). I'll correlate with the oncall incident notes.
infra-bot: incident updated: incident-telemetry-ingest-2140012345 state=investigating owner=Mia Chen
Mia Chen: also — billing/cs heads want a short note about customer impact. Paul, can you stub a 2-sentence customer-facing line?
Paul Rivers: "We observed transient ingestion latency affecting a subset of telemetry uploads; we implemented smoothing and routing mitigations. No lasting data loss; we will follow up with quota options for heavy senders."
Devin Patel: small add — recommend offering a short-term ingestion bundle for enterprise tenants who need higher throughput guarantees.
Mia Chen: perfect. thanks all, will close when PRs land and oncall clears incident.
